items.title: Freeze the seven-capability ledger and coverage audit
items.context: Create an original intent snapshot, milestone ledger, and initial coverage table for all seven capabilities. Verify whether B-cd3a, B-edb8, or earlier stories already cover any row before implementation.

happy.desc: Audit maps all seven requested capability rows to an explicit resolution state before any row is marked done.

edge.desc: Audit distinguishes already-covered, partial, missing, implemented, and retired/non-goal instead of collapsing partial rows into done.

adversarial.desc: No capability row can be omitted from the audit while B-c004 still claims full completion.

items.userSees: The final status table shows CHK-001/M1 with a committed seven-row audit and no omitted capability rows.

items.title: Retire active Authority Server future backlog language
items.context: Authority Server conformance is no longer an active capability. Update active docs/tests so Authority Server language is legacy/retired compatibility only, not future work or remaining capability.

happy.desc: Active Authority Server future backlog language is removed or rewritten as retired legacy compatibility.

edge.desc: Canonical local/shadow consumer names that still include compatibility vocabulary are explicitly bounded and not described as server production readiness.

adversarial.desc: A guard fails if the two referenced decision docs reintroduce Authority Server conformance as active future work.

items.title: Resolve Tier-C cleanup policy
items.context: Determine whether automated Tier-C cleanup is needed. If not, retire it as a non-goal with tests proving valid Tier-C experiments are preserved and malformed Tier-C-like rows remain cleanup-required.

happy.desc: Tier-C cleanup policy is explicitly implemented or explicitly retired as a non-goal with current control-plane status aligned.

edge.desc: Valid Tier-C experiment batches remain preserved and are not classified as ordinary duplicates to delete.

adversarial.desc: Malformed Tier-C-like rows remain cleanup-required and cannot hide behind the experiment exception.

items.title: Resolve append-only admissibility ledger capability
items.context: Verify whether evaluator plus waterline is sufficient. If durable ledger remains required, implement it; otherwise formally downgrade to non-goal with tests preventing accidental claims of ledger completion.

happy.desc: Append-only admissibility ledger is either implemented under .lattice/evidence with durable tests or formally retired/downgraded while waterline remains diagnostic-only.

edge.desc: Diagnostic waterline output cannot be mistaken for append-only durable ledger storage or DONE evidence.

adversarial.desc: A proof consumer cannot mutate or overwrite prior admissibility rows if a ledger is implemented, or cannot claim ledger support if it is retired.

items.title: Complete queue cleanup enforcement guard
items.context: Add or verify hard guards for duplicate/superseded cleanup mutation paths while preserving experiment exceptions and surfacing malformed cleanup-required rows.

happy.desc: Queue cleanup enforcement guard blocks or classifies duplicate/superseded/cleanup-required mutation paths according to policy.

edge.desc: Tier-C experiment exceptions remain preserved and do not get deleted by ordinary duplicate cleanup behavior.

adversarial.desc: Cleanup-required rows cannot be marked preserved merely by spoofing a Tier-C-like title or metadata fragment.

items.title: Complete runtime closure enforce rollout
items.context: Move configured runtime enforcement from partial/warn-only to a verified enforce rollout where appropriate, with rollback documented as lifecycleControl.runtimeEnforcement=warn and tests for wrong cwd, stale lock, dirty tree, and worktree authority drift.

happy.desc: Runtime closure enforcement behavior is verified in warn and enforce modes, with rollback path documented.

edge.desc: Global status does not overclaim default hard enforcement when config is still warn.

adversarial.desc: Unsafe runtime closure findings block lifecycle transition when enforce mode is configured.

items.title: Complete CommandSpec envelope and project waterline coverage
items.context: Audit command-backed evidence surfaces, migrate missing gate-consumed command evidence to structured CommandSpec where needed, and complete project-level consumption waterline rollup without making the waterline proof authority.

happy.desc: Gate-consumed command evidence surfaces have CommandSpec envelope coverage or explicit non-goal notes, and project-level consumption waterline rollup reports real aggregate state.

edge.desc: Project waterline with no story rows is distinguished from passing green status.

adversarial.desc: A receipt-like command evidence row without a CommandSpec envelope cannot be treated as strong proof for high-risk consumers.
